book.unit_title: Squares, Square Roots, Cubes and Cube Roots

title: Square of a rational number
competency: Calculate the square of a number.

keywords.def: A number multiplied by itself: a² = a × a.
A rational number x with x = m² for some rational m, like 9 = 3² or 1/25 = (1/5)².
Changing a number to a simpler, nearby value: look at the next digit; less than 5 round down, 5 or more round up.

en.text: Squaring means multiplying a number by itself: a² = a × a. Read a² as "a squared". For a fraction, square the top and the bottom. A negative number squared is positive. Do not mix up a² with 2a.

am.text: ማካሬ ማለት ቁጥርን በራሱ ማባዛት ነው፤ a² = a × a። ለክፍልፋይ ላዩንና ታቹን አካሬ። አሉታዊ ቁጥር ሲካሬ አዎንታዊ ይሆናል። a² ከ 2a ጋር አንድ አይደለም።

screens.title: Tiling a room
screens.ask: A square room is 4 m long and 4 m wide. How many 1 m × 1 m tiles cover the floor?
screens.after: 4 rows of 4 tiles: 4 × 4 = 16 tiles. 4 × 4 is called "4 squared", written 4².

screens.title: Activity 2.1
screens.intro: A square with sides of 3 units. Fill it row by row.
say: The first row has 3 small squares.

screens.title: Squaring
paras: Definition 2.1: Multiplying a number by itself is called squaring the number.
If a is multiplied by itself, the product is written a².
We read a² as "a squared", "the square of a" or "a to the power of 2".

screens.title: a² is not 2a
outs: a² = a × a (area of the square)
screens.note: Move the slider. a² grows much faster than 2a. They are equal only when a = 2 (or a = 0).

screens.title: a² is not 2a
paras: a² = a × a, but 2a = a + a.
screens.note: For a fraction: (a/b)² = a²/b², where b ≠ 0. For a product: (ab)² = a²b².

screens.title: Key words
defs: A number multiplied by itself: a² = a × a.

screens.title: Square 4/3 and −10/16
steps: Simplify: GCF of 100 and 256 is 4. 100 ÷ 4 = 25 and 256 ÷ 4 = 64.

screens.why:
6² means 6 × 6 (six multiplied by itself).
6 × 6 = 36.
12 is 6 × 2, which is 2 × 6, not 6².
screens.clue: 6² means 6 × 6, not 6 × 2.

screens.why:
Step 1: (−20)² means (−20) × (−20).
Step 2: sign: negative × negative = positive.
Step 3: size: 20 × 20 = 400.
So (−20)² = +400.
screens.clue: Multiply −20 by itself. What sign do two negatives give?

screens.why:
Step 1: change to an improper fraction: 3 1/4 = (3 × 4 + 1)/4 = 13/4.
Step 2: square the top: 13 × 13 = 169.
Step 3: square the bottom: 4 × 4 = 16.
So (13/4)² = 169/16.
Step 4: 169 ÷ 16 = 10 remainder 9, so 169/16 = 10 9/16.
Careful: (3 1/4)² is NOT 9 1/16. You must square the whole number 13/4.
screens.clue: First change 3 1/4 to an improper fraction.

screens.why:
Step 1: ignore the point: 3 × 3 = 9.
Step 2: count decimal places: 0.03 has 2, so 0.03 × 0.03 has 2 + 2 = 4.
Step 3: write 9 with 4 decimal places: 0.0009.
Check: 3/100 × 3/100 = 9/10000 = 0.0009.
screens.clue: Count the decimal places: 2 + 2.

screens.why:
8² means 8 × 8 = 64.
8 × 2 = 16.
64 ≠ 16, so the statement is false. a² is not the same as 2a.
screens.clue: Squaring means multiplying a number by itself.

screens.ask: Area of a square = side × side. A square has sides of 9 cm. Area = ___ cm²
screens.why:
The area of a square is side × side = side².
9 × 9 = 81.
So the area is 81 cm² (square centimetres).
screens.clue: Area of a square = side × side.

screens.text: Brackets matter! Which one is equal to 3600?
screens.why:
(−60)² squares −60: (−60) × (−60) = +3600.
−60² squares only 60, then puts a minus in front: −(60 × 60) = −3600.
60 × 2 = 120.
So only (−60)² equals 3600.
screens.clue: Brackets matter. Which one squares the −60?

screens.text: Spot the mistake. Kebede says (2/3)² = 4/6. What went wrong?
opts: He squared the top only. The answer is 4/9.
screens.ans: He squared the top only. The answer is 4/9.
screens.why:
(2/3)² = 2/3 × 2/3.
Tops: 2 × 2 = 4. Bottoms: 3 × 3 = 9.
So (2/3)² = 4/9.
Kebede wrote 6 on the bottom: he did 3 × 2 instead of 3 × 3.
screens.clue: Square the top AND the bottom.

en.text: A perfect square is a number you get by squaring a rational number: 1, 4, 9, 16, 1/25, 0.04. Adding the first n odd numbers always gives n²: 1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2n − 1) = n². The square of an even number is even; the square of an odd number is odd.

am.text: ፍጹም ካሬ ምክንያታዊ ቁጥርን በማካሬ የሚገኝ ቁጥር ነው፤ ለምሳሌ 1፣ 4፣ 9፣ 16። የመጀመሪያዎቹ n ጎዶሎ ቁጥሮች ድምር n² ነው።

screens.title: Group work 2.1
screens.after: 16. Look: 1, 4, 9, 16 are 1², 2², 3², 4². The sums of odd numbers are squares! Build it below.

screens.title: Why it works
paras: Each new odd number wraps an L shape around the square.
To grow an n × n square into (n + 1) × (n + 1), you add an L of 2n + 1 squares: the next odd number.
So the first n odd numbers always fill an n × n square.
screens.note: The n-th odd number is 2n − 1. For n = 10 it is 19, and 1 + 3 + … + 19 = 10² = 100.

screens.title: Perfect squares
paras: Definition 2.2: A rational number x is a perfect square if x = m² for some rational m.
screens.note: The square of a rational number is rational. 0² = 0.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A rational number x with x = m² for some rational m, like 9 = 3² or 1/25 = (1/5)².

screens.text: Perfect squares: which of these can be written as a number × itself?
screens.why:
4 = 2 × 2, 16 = 4 × 4, 0.04 = 0.2 × 0.2, 1/4 = 1/2 × 1/2.
12 is between 3² = 9 and 4² = 16, so no whole number squared gives 12.
18 is between 4² = 16 and 5² = 25, so it is not a perfect square either.
screens.clue: Can you write each as something × itself?

screens.ask: Use the odd-number pattern: the sum of the first 15 odd numbers = ___
screens.why:
Rule: the first n odd numbers add up to n².
Here n = 15, so the sum is 15² = 15 × 15 = 225.
Check: the 15th odd number is 2 × 15 − 1 = 29, and 1 + 3 + … + 29 = 225.
screens.clue: Use the pattern: first n odd numbers add up to n².

screens.text: Is 201 a perfect square? Compare it with the squares near it.
screens.why:
14² = 196 and 15² = 225.
196 < 201 < 225, so 201 is between two squares next to each other.
No whole number squared gives 201.
Being odd does not decide it: 225 is odd and is a perfect square.
screens.clue: Find the squares just below and just above 201.

screens.why:
Step 1: 38² = 38 × 38 = 1444.
Step 2: 37² = 37 × 37 = 1369.
Step 3: 1444 − 1369 = 75.
Pattern: the answer is 38 + 37 = 75. In general (n + 1)² − n² = 2n + 1.
screens.clue: Square each number first, then subtract.

screens.text: True or false? The square of an even number is always even.
screens.why:
An even number is 2 × something, e.g. 14 = 2 × 7.
Its square is 2 × 2 × 7 × 7, which still has the factor 2.
So it is even: 14² = 196, 20² = 400.
screens.clue: Try 2², 4², 6².

screens.text: Which number is the square of an odd number?
screens.why:
529 = 23 × 23, and 23 is odd.
196 = 14², 484 = 22², 400 = 20²: all squares of even numbers.
Quick test: an odd number squared is odd, and 529 is the only odd choice.
screens.clue: An odd number squared is odd.

screens.ask: Abel adds odd numbers 1 + 3 + 5 + … and gets 400. How many odd numbers did he add? ___
screens.why:
The first n odd numbers add up to n².
So n² = 400.
Which number times itself is 400? 20 × 20 = 400.
So Abel added 20 odd numbers (the last one is 2 × 20 − 1 = 39).
screens.clue: Which number squared gives 400?

en.text: To estimate a square quickly, round the number first, then square it. 4.3 ≈ 4, so (4.3)² ≈ 16. Rounding: if the next digit is less than 5 round down; if it is 5 or more round up.

am.text: ካሬን በፍጥነት ለመገመት መጀመሪያ ቁጥሩን አጠጋጋ፣ ከዚያ አካሬ። 4.3 ≈ 4፣ ስለዚህ (4.3)² ≈ 16።

screens.title: Quick guess
screens.ask: Without working it out: is (4.3)² closer to 16 or to 25?
screens.after: 4.3 is close to 4, and 4² = 16. Exactly, (4.3)² = 18.49, which is near 16.

screens.title: How to approximate a square
paras: Rounding gives a quick estimate of a square.
Look at the next digit to the right.
If it is less than 5, round down. If it is 5 or more, round up.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Changing a number to a simpler, nearby value: look at the next digit; less than 5 round down, 5 or more round up.

screens.title: Estimate (10.8)²
steps: Look at the digit after the point: 8.
8 is 5 or more, so round up: 10.8 ≈ 11.

screens.text: Estimate by rounding to a whole number first: (4.2)² is about
screens.why:
Step 1: round 4.2. The digit after the point is 2, and 2 < 5, so round down: 4.
Step 2: square: 4² = 16.
17.64 is the exact value, not an estimate.
screens.clue: Round 4.2 to a whole number first.

screens.why:
Step 1: round −8.7: the digit 7 is 5 or more, so −8.7 ≈ −9.
Step 2: square: (−9) × (−9) = 81.
Two negatives make a positive. Exactly, (−8.7)² = 75.69.
screens.clue: Round to −9, then square. Two negatives make a positive.

screens.why:
(9.9)² = 9.9 × 9.9 = 98.01.
Rounding 9.9 to 10 gives (9.9)² ≈ 100, but "about" is not "equal".
So the statement is false.
screens.clue: Is "about" the same as "equal"?
Work out each value and compare.

screens.text: Hana estimates (6.4)² ≈ 36. The exact value is 40.96. Why is her estimate too small?
screens.why:
6.4 ≈ 6, because the digit 4 is less than 5.
6 is smaller than 6.4, so 6² = 36 is smaller than 6.4² = 40.96.
Rounding down always gives an estimate below the exact square.
screens.clue: Is 6 bigger or smaller than 6.4?

items.why:
4.5² = 4.5 × 4.5.
Without the points: 45 × 45 = 2025.
4.5 has 1 decimal place, so the product has 1 + 1 = 2: 20.25.

(−5/4)² = (−5/4) × (−5/4).
Sign: negative × negative = positive.
Tops: 5 × 5 = 25. Bottoms: 4 × 4 = 16.
So x² = 25/16 = 1 9/16.
items.clue: Square the top and the bottom. The sign becomes +.

items.why:
Simplify first: GCF of 12 and 4 is 4, so 12/4 = 3.
Then 3² = 3 × 3 = 9.
Or: (12/4)² = 144/16 = 9.

items.text: Use prime factors: is 324 a square number?
items.why:
324 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3.
Make two equal groups: (2 × 3 × 3) × (2 × 3 × 3) = 18 × 18.
So 324 = 18², a square number.

items.ask: Write 64 as the sum of the first eight odd numbers: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 13 + ___
items.why:
64 = 8², so it is the sum of the first 8 odd numbers.
The 8th odd number is 2 × 8 − 1 = 15.
Check: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 13 + 15 = 64.
items.clue: List the first eight odd numbers.

items.why:
0² = 0 × 0 = 0.
Zero times anything is zero, so 0² is 0, not 2.

items.ask: Estimate x² by rounding to a whole number. x = 10.8, so x² ≈ ___
items.why:
10.8 → the digit 8 is 5 or more → round up to 11.
11² = 121.
So x² ≈ 121 (exactly 116.64).
items.clue: Round to the nearest whole number first.

items.ask: Estimate x² by rounding to one decimal place. x = 1.06, so x² ≈ ___
items.why:
1.06 → the digit after the first decimal is 6, so round up to 1.1.
(1.1)² = 1.1 × 1.1 = 1.21.
So x² ≈ 1.21 (exactly 1.1236).

test.why:
0.09 = 0.3 × 0.3 = (0.3)².
50, 20 and 1/8 cannot be written as a rational number times itself.

test.ask: Use the odd-number pattern: the sum of the first 12 odd numbers = ___
test.why:
First n odd numbers add up to n².
12² = 144.

notes.text: Activity 2.1 Q1: the figure labels are misprinted (b and c printed together next to the 3 × 3 grid). Read as 1 × 1, 3 × 3, 4 × 4, 5 × 5 unit squares.
Page 45 note says "a² ≠ 2a for any rational number a". This fails for a = 0 and a = 2; the book means "in general". The slider shows this.
Exercise 2.1 Q1 d "−60² = 3600" is false as printed (−60² = −3600). If (−60)² was meant, it is true. Used as an mcq that contrasts both.

screens.text: Top × top, bottom × bottom, then simplify.

screens.why:
Step 1: multiply the tops: 3 × 3 = 9.
Step 2: multiply the bottoms: 5 × 5 = 25.
So 3/5 × 3/5 = 9/25.
screens.clue: Multiply the tops, then the bottoms.

screens.title: Round 4.3 and 2.45
screens.text: Look at the next digit to the right.
steps: 4.3 to a whole number: the next digit is 3. 3 < 5, so round down: 4.
2.45 to one decimal place: the next digit is 5. 5 or more, so round up: 2.5.

screens.text: Round 10.8 to the nearest whole number.
screens.why:
Look at the digit after the point: 8.
8 is 5 or more, so round up.
10.8 → 11.
screens.clue: Is the digit after the point less than 5?
